_: Kill-check for asc-09wx.14 stage G5: a tree that passed the gate is not gated again. This module exists to answer 'already passed', and the severity-zero defect is answering it for a tree that did not pass -- a green verdict nobody earned destroys the value of every other green verdict. So the mutants are one per way the module could answer wrongly: remembering a FAILED run (M1, the plan's own mutant), keying on something that collapses the amend case (M2, the plan's other), and then one per fail-closed rule -- the checkout, the schema version, the step list, and the two env guards that keep a run which asked for everything from being answered out of a record (M6, M7). Every killer was FOUND, not guessed: each mutant was planted in the working tree and scripts/gate-memo.test.ts run with --reporter=json, and the failing names were read off assertionResults. Measured 2026-10-13. NOTE for anyone adding a mutant here, and it was MEASURED rather than reasoned about: a find/replace that leaves the module with a SYNTAX ERROR makes vitest fail the whole file at COLLECTION, so `assertionResults` is EMPTY and `numFailedTests` is 0 while the parse error sits in `testResults[].message`. An author finding killers by hand -- the documented method is to apply the mutant, run the owning test file with --reporter=json and read the failing names off assertionResults -- therefore sees NO failing test and reads a mutant that cannot load as a survivor. Check that the mutant PARSES (`node --check <file>`) before believing any survivor. THIS RUNNER DOES NOT HAVE THAT GAP: it reads vitest's summary line (executed()), so the same mutant reports `DEAD KILLER -- the file ran no test`, quotes the parse error, and counts as a problem. M7's first spelling deleted the guarded line outright, which left `&&` before the closing paren and produced exactly this; it was respelled to `true` for that reason. Measured 2026-10-13 (dogfood/0094, asc-funq). RESPUN 2026-10-14 (dogfood/0099): the memo stopped being refused wholesale under `ASCEND_PRECOMMIT_FULL` -- one `but push` of a two-branch stack had paid this gate twice, once per branch, because git runs the pre-push hook once per push command -- and the guard moved from that flag into a bar the caller sets, `requiredOf` in scripts/gate.mjs. M6 and M7 were respelled against the new lines, and M8/M9 were added as the two directions of that bar: M8 drops it, so a push is answered by a commit's record; M9 turns it into full coverage, which is the first draft's rule and vetoes every amend there is -- the measurement the memo module's own docblock records.
